name: Today's Report
headline: Mortgage applications rose 3.4% last week as rates eased, but home purchase applications are still 18% behind last year's pace.
teaser: Mortgage applications rose 3.4% as rates eased, but purchase applications trail last year by 18%, and Alameda County's fell 6.9% in 2025. The Fed held rates at 3.75% to 4.00%.

sections.label: Real estate
sections.html:
Buyers are pausing, not leaving. The Mortgage Bankers Association's weekly survey, out this morning, shows mortgage applications up 3.4% in the week ending October 23 as its 30-year contract rate eased to 7.37% from 7.41%. Even with that bounce, home purchase applications were 18% below the same week last year, and refinances were 61% lower.

Rates explain most of it. Early this year, with that rate near 6.2%, purchase applications ran as much as 18% ahead of 2025. Then rates rose every week for two months, reaching 7.50% in early October, the highest since November 2023, and purchase applications have trailed last year in each of the past seven weeks. More borrowers are choosing adjustable rate loans, now 11.3% of applications, the most in over a year.

Here at home. The newest full year of federal lending data (HMDA) shows Alameda County lenders took 13,940 home purchase loan applications in 2025, down 6.9% from 2024 even as the nation edged up 1.1%, and about half the 2021 peak. Our own MLS shows the same pause today: on this date a year apart, across the same 14 cities, homes in contract fell 26% to 609 from 820, while homes for sale barely moved, 1,957 from 1,989.

What it means for you. If you are buying, get pre-approved now so you can move when rates dip; this week showed how fast buyers come back on even a small one. If a lender offers an adjustable rate loan, make sure you understand how and when the rate can change. If you are selling, price for today's payment from day one: inventory is about where it was a year ago, but a quarter fewer homes are going into contract.

Rates and the Fed. Mortgage News Daily's 30-year average held at 7.33% Tuesday and the 15-year is 7.01%. At 11 AM Pacific the Fed left its target range at 3.75% to 4.00% (more in Economy).

Today's count. Board wide: 2,554 listings across the 15 city table, counting active and in contract together, down from 2,578, with 144 coming soon and 148 brand new. The five city ledger carries 674 live listings across Fremont, Hayward, Milpitas, Newark and Union City, 605 on the market and 69 coming soon, down from 678.

Fremont holds 226 live listings: 184 active, 28 coming soon and 14 brand new, with a median on market list price of $1,299,944 at $801 a square foot and a typical listing out 35 days. Hayward carries 196 (from 198), Milpitas 103 (from 104), Newark 89 (unchanged) and Union City 60 (from 61). Across all five cities the median is $1,079,000 at $668 a square foot, 283 homes are priced under a million, and 182 have been sitting 60 days or longer.

images.alt: Bar chart of home purchase loan applications in Alameda County by year: 22,624 in 2018, 21,382 in 2019, 20,827 in 2020, a peak of 26,227 in 2021, 20,669 in 2022, 14,713 in 2023, 14,973 in 2024 and 13,940 in 2025. A side panel compares 2025: Alameda County was down 6.9% from 2024 while the United States was up 1.1%, and down 34.8% from 2019 against 16.3% for the United States.
images.caption: Alameda County lenders took 13,940 home purchase loan applications in 2025, about half the 2021 peak and 35% fewer than in 2019. Nationally, 2025 was 16% below 2019.

sections.label: Economy
sections.html:
The Fed holds. At 11 AM Pacific the Fed left its target range at 3.75% to 4.00%, after raising it in September. Two policymakers, Lisa Cook and Beth Hammack, voted against the decision because they wanted another quarter point increase. Mortgage rates follow the 10-Year Treasury more closely than the Fed's own rate, and the 10-Year closed Tuesday at 4.99%, just under 5%.

Oil slips, metals firm. Brent's December contract settled at $113.88, down 1.67%, though it is up 1.81% this morning. Gold rose 1.04% to $4,073 and silver 0.85% to $54.50. The numbers above are Tuesday's Treasury close, COMEX December gold and silver at the 4 PM ET print, and the ICE December Brent settlement.

sections.label: Stocks
sections.html: Inching up before the Fed. The numbers above are Tuesday's closes, led by the Nasdaq's 1.18% gain; as of 10:07 AM PT the S&P 500 is up 0.24%, the Dow up 0.30% and the Nasdaq up 0.06%. The Fed held rates steady at 11 AM Pacific, and Microsoft reports its quarter today.

sections.label: Crypto
sections.html: Flat into the Fed. Bitcoin is down 0.07% over 24 hours near $80,400, Ether is down 0.66% and XRP is down 0.53%, live from CoinGecko at 10:07 AM PT. Home buyers and Bitcoin holders rarely agree on anything, but both got the same answer from the Fed at 11 AM: no change.
